chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Concerning a woman whose menstrual blood ceases at the end of her days, he said: “If her husband is overcome by desire, then let him instruct her, and let her wash her private part; then he may touch her, if he wishes, before she performs ghusl (ritual bath).”
As for the reports which ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated that intercourse with her is not permissible except after ghusl (ritual bath), such as...

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath relevant to post-menstrual purity
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman under discussion in the legal ruling
key_terms.دَمُ الْحَيْضَةِ: menstrual blood whose cessation determines the ruling
key_terms.شَبَقٌ: intense sexual desire affecting the husband
key_terms.فَرْجَهَا: her private part, which she is instructed to wash
key_terms.يَمَسُّهَا: he may approach or touch her sexually

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to have intercourse after menstrual bleeding stops but before ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling regarding a woman whose menstruation has ended but who has not yet performed ghusl (ritual bath). It indicates permissibility for the husband to approach her after she washes her private part, even before ghusl, while also introducing other reports that appear to require ghusl first.
